newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares dip 2.6 pct, auto firms worst hit.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares dip 2.6 pct, auto firms worst hit.

text.p: Bombay shares slid 2.5 percent on Friday as funds and punters sold on disappointing first half earnings announcements and gloomy industrial growth data, traders said.

Bombay's benchmark stocks index dropped 75.83 points or 2.5 percent to a provisional close of 2967.47. The 50-share index of the National Stock Exchange dipped 19.54 points or 2.25 percent to a provisional 850.46.
Traders said shares of index stocks Tata Chemicals and IDBI took a pounding after their first half results fell below market expectations.
Tata Chemicals shares fell 14.75 rupees or 8.16 percent to 166 after the firm said on Wednesday its net profit for the six months to September 1996 fell below the year-ago.
IDBI shares dropped 10.25 rupees or 9.93 percent after the finance firm said on Thursday its net profit rose a modest 2.0 percent during the first half.

Traders said fears of a slowdown in the economy -- confirmed by latest government data released on Wednesday -- added to the gloom. India's April-September industrial growth has slowed to 4.8 percent from 12.8 percent during the corresponding period last year.
Shares of auto firms were hit when a couple of funds turned sellers in TELCO and Bajaj Auto. Punters used rumours of poor October auto sales to pull prices of these stocks lower.
But some auto analysts said sales had not shown a slowdown from the year-ago.

"TELCO's total sales for October are at 16,822 vehicles, up 26.2 percent from the year-ago and down 5.2 percent from September which is traditionally when sales peak," said an auto analyst at a foreign brokerage firm, quoting unofficial figures.
Official auto figures for October are due early next week.
The analyst said Bajaj sales were at 120,389 in October, up 16 percent from the year-ago and up 1.8 percent from September.
